children: Just a year after the conglomerate privatised its tourism unit that included the resort chain for $1.2 bln, it is now relisting ClubMed as a standalone business. That's sensible. But bagging a similar valuation as faster-growing, more profitable hotel chains will be tough.

Fosun International plans to spin off the operator of its ClubMed resort brand for a Hong Kong initial public offering, the Chinese conglomerate said in a stock exchange filing on August 28. The listing vehicle, ClubMed Lifestyle Group, plans to expand its global resort network to about 85 locations by 2030 from 69 now.
Fosun is planning to list ClubMed in Hong Kong in a deal that could raise more than $500 million, Reuters reported on May 19, citing a source with knowledge of the matter.
